title: One Ångström Inside the Retrovirus That Rewrote the Central Dogma — Peyton Rous's 1911 Berkefeld Filtrate, Temin & Baltimore's 1970 Reverse Transcriptase, Stehelin–Varmus–Bishop's c-Src, HIV-1 RT AZT/Tenofovir (PDB 1RTD, 3V4I, 1T05) & c-Src pTyr527 Clamp (PDB 2SRC, 1Y57)

teenKit.tldr: A single sick chicken in 1909 sparked a 60-year scientific war, proving that viruses can rewrite our genetic code and cause cancer.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how viruses and rogue genes hack our cells is the exact foundation that gave us modern targeted cancer therapies and turned HIV from a death sentence into a manageable condition.
keyTakeaways: Peyton Rous discovered that a cell-free liquid filtered from a chicken tumor could cause cancer in healthy birds, defying the dogma that cancer wasn't contagious.
Howard Temin's radical DNA provirus hypothesis—ridiculed for years—was ultimately proven by the discovery of Reverse Transcriptase, an enzyme that turns RNA back into DNA.
Researchers discovered that cancer-causing genes (oncogenes) aren't alien invaders, but normal cellular genes (like c-Src) that were hijacked and mutated by viruses.

vocab.meaning: A type of virus that stores its genetic instructions in single-stranded RNA and uses a special enzyme to copy them into the host's DNA.
The molecular machine inside retroviruses that breaks the old biological rulebook by translating RNA backward into DNA.
A gene that has the potential to cause cancer when mutated or expressed at abnormally high levels.
A normal, healthy gene that helps control cell growth and division, which can turn into a cancer-causing oncogene if stolen or broken.

quiz.question: What was the prevailing medical consensus about cancer when Peyton Rous received the Plymouth Rock hen in 1909?
options: It was universally known to be caused by retroviruses.
It was strictly a local cellular disease that could not be transmitted between organisms.
It was entirely caused by bacterial infections.
It was a purely genetic condition inherited only from parents.
quiz.explanation: Pathologists at the time believed cancer was just an isolated rogue cell dividing out of force, making Rous's discovery of a transmissible agent revolutionary and highly controversial.

quiz.question: Why did Howard Temin face years of ridicule from the scientific community after proposing his DNA provirus hypothesis in 1964?
options: He claimed that chicken RNA could be eaten to cure diseases.
He suggested that RNA could be copied backward into DNA, directly violating the Central Dogma of molecular biology.
He used microscopes that were proven to be entirely fictional.
He argued that viruses had nothing to do with cancer whatsoever.
quiz.explanation: At the time, the Central Dogma dictated that genetic information only flowed one way: from DNA to RNA to proteins, making Temin's idea of backward copying heretical.

quiz.question: What did Stehelin, Varmus, and Bishop discover about the v-src gene found in viruses?
options: It was an alien sequence brought to Earth by meteorites.
It was manufactured entirely by synthetic lab chemicals in 1976.
It was actually stolen from normal vertebrate host genomes, proving viruses can hijack regular genes.
It had no relation to cancer and only affected bird feathers.
quiz.explanation: They proved that the cancer-causing gene in the virus (v-src) was actually a corrupted version of a normal, helpful gene (c-Src) stolen from the host animal's own DNA.
